Library to Extend Weekend Hours After Petition

Posted Thursday, October 16, 2026 4:12 pm | Staff report
Advertisement

Starting in November, the main branch of the Valley Public Library will open on Sundays from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m., the library board decided on Wednesday. The change follows a petition signed by more than 2,300 residents, many of them parents and students who said Saturday hours were not enough.

Board president Alma Reyes said the extra day will be covered by reshuffling existing staff, so no new positions are needed for now. Two part-time clerks have agreed to move their shifts, and volunteers from the Friends of the Library group will help run the children’s room.

The petition was started in June by a high school junior, Daniel Kim, who said he often had nowhere quiet to study on weekends. “I just wanted somewhere to sit with my books,” he said, adding that he was surprised by how quickly the signatures came in.

Weekday hours will not change, but the evening closing time on Fridays will move from 8 p.m. to 6 p.m. to balance the budget. Library staff said Friday evenings are the quietest time of the week, with fewer than thirty visitors on most nights.

The board will review attendance in March, and it may extend Sunday hours to the two smaller branches if demand holds up. Residents can comment on the plan at the next public meeting, which is listed on the events calendar.
